correctness.rationale: For every n>=5, the natural S_n action on unordered ground pairs is the full Kneser automorphism group. Fixing every selected two-subset is equivalent to all ground incidence signatures being distinct. This is equivalent precisely to at most one isolated ground vertex and no isolated K2 component. The labeled component-exclusion exponential formula yields the full fixing polynomial with factor (1+t)e^{-t-zt^2/2}, and n![t^n] gives unquotiented labeled graphs. The extremal component lower bound forces forests and the listed residue-class size profiles. Labeled Cayley-tree counts prove exact minimum multiplicities; exhaustive direct checks independently confirm n=5..7 all coefficients, n=8..9 minimum coefficients and closed coefficients through n=21. The proof states n>=5 and does not treat finite experiments as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Directly read primary graph fixing-polynomial and Kneser base-size sources, including Kneser separation and hypergraph lemmas, and compare their actual implications. The selected-edge feasibility rule and scalar optimum are covered by earlier results, but the complete labeled all-size polynomial and explicit three-residue classification with minimum-base multiplicities were not stated or provided by the inspected theorems. Targeted literature and published-record checks found no such enumerator; unindexed equivalent enumeration remains a real risk.
residual_risks: The exact Kneser feasibility criterion is old; specialized enumeration may be implicitly accessible from prior hypergraph constructions or folklore.
Unindexed earlier counting work under permutation bases, separating systems, fixing polynomials, or incidence-distinct graphs could already contain the same EGF or labeled minimum counts.
No independent review or exhaustive search over every publication and unpublished result has been performed.

value.rationale: The fixing polynomial is a previously motivated all-cardinality symmetry-breaking invariant (Javaid et al. 2017), not an arbitrary isolated numerical slice. The result classifies every determining set for the natural infinite family K(n,2) and exactly enumerates its labeled optimal bases by n mod 3, refining published scalar determining-number theorems. The coefficient data measure how many distinct minimum sensor/coordinate choices exist, information a minimum cardinality alone cannot supply. No claim of a paper-sized application is needed.
